posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
So, in a different thread (this one), we were talking about creepy characters.  
In it, I expounded on my theory about Spite's prediliction for getting people to trust him- that betraying that trust was as important to him as the kill.
 
This led me to start thinking about F6 Wraith's incapacitated side- where (if you haven't seen it) Spite is about to throw the Wraith over a railing to an uncertain (but probably not good) fate.  
 
see- theres two things about it that seem odd to me.
 
First, Spite is in a costume.  He's not in a hoodie that can give him some ability to blend in.  
Second, the Wraith looks surprised. Think about that.
 
See, I'm wondering if Spite pulled off the ultimate betrayal of trust.  In Iron Legacy's timeline, we don't know if Spite ever became the drugged out lunatic. 
We also know that IL was NOT kind to villains- and spite (due to the ravages of the drugs) was not subtle at the end, when he started overdosing and raiding labs.  
 
What if Spite convinced the others that he was a hero?  Someone who wanted to help them fight Iron Legacy for the greater good?
 
Maybe he met Maia in the fighting pits she was in.  She's distrustful, but he saves her life several times (and if he used too much force, its a bad future and everyone has to do things they don't want to do).
 
He slowly- very slowly- convinces her that he's a hero.
All so that when he gets her alone and she finally trusts him, he can betray her and send her plummeting to her death.

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Thats the thing that got me thinking.  ALL the incaps have to happen, though they don't always happen in the order you'd expect, or mean what you'd think.  Now, some of them definitely ARE homages, but they also have to be the results of a series of events.

Think about Ambuscade.  We see him shooting Team Leader Tachyon in her incap side... but how did that series of events actually happen? Why did Iron Legacy leave him alive in the first place?  Was he hunting superhumans FOR Iron Legacy?  Was he some kind of leader of the superpowered resistance movement, hunting Iron Legacy and doing whatever was necessary to retain his cover?  

 

In terms of Spite, if he's a known (and quite unrepentant) serial killer, how could he possibly still be alive?   If he was as out of control as (main timeline) Spite became, it seems ludicrous that Iron Legacy wouldn't have put him down, particularly since he preyed on children (among others).

posts.cooked:
I think you might be giving IL a bit too much credit in terms of morality and restraint.  He killed Tyler.  

What I'm gettting at isn't so much about who Iron legacy chooses to kill, its more that the world in which he inhabits is a MUCH more brutal one.  Life is a lot cheaper and the heroes have been through some horrific trials.  Some of them are dead.

In that atmosphere, and in that world, it seems likely that some of the villains must have changed their routines.  Because if they didn't- if they carreid on the same way as they did in the normal timeline- they would get put down.  Maybe they'd end up in prison...but they sure as heck wouldn't be free to wreak havoc.

thats why I find Spite's appearance on the incap so bizarre.  In the main timeline, theres a degree of mercy in the heroes.  But in the F6 world- where the heroes ave seen so much crumble around them, I just don't see him surviving any length of time behaving the same way he behaved in the main timeline.

posts.cooked: My be reference for comparison of a superhuman serial killer is Sylar from Heroes (before he went all pear-shaped in the later seasons - everything did, but most especially him).  When being a psychopath is just too dangerous to get away with, it's extremely easy for them to tuck their nastiness away in a corner and blend in; lying comes naturally do them, they can always behave themselves and even go the extra mile creating a disguise, being more perfect than the actual Good people, because all the time they're just reminding themselves of the "fun" they get to have later.
